patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Linear only if your buying job matches “Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo ” rather than Wrike's shape. Choose Wrike only if your buying job matches “Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/use” rather than Linear's shape. Workflow advantage: Linear leans shared coverage; Wrike leans resource-planning, team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Linear is Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo annual.; Wrike is Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Linear (startup, small-business, mid-market) vs Wrike (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Linear-leaning — vs Wrike-leaning resource-planning, team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Linear — Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Wrike — Business tier pricing jump.

Limitations — Linear: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise; Wrike: Business tier pricing jump; Heavier admin than lightweight tools.

Poor-fit cases: Linear is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS · Wrike is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Business tier pricing jump · Avoid Linear if you actually need Wrike's motion (Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team fr)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
